t: Create and publish games and places
d: Explains how to create, publish, and release games.
h:
import PlaceSizeLimit from '../../includes/place-size-limit.md'

When you open Studio and create a new game, your project starts with a single place that players load into when they first join the game. Games can have one or multiple places that each contain all components for that portion of the game, including its specific environment, 3D objects, and scripts.

Places are comparable to scenes in Unity or maps in Unreal Engine.

Many creators create additional places within a game to organize assets for different gameplay areas. For example, if you want players to join a dungeon before teleporting to either a vast desert or spooky island, you can organize the assets for each area into their own place.

Every place is represented by a data model that stores and organizes:

  • All objects that make up the 3D world of a place, such as its parts, meshes, terrain, and lighting.
  • All objects that can control runtime behavior, such as scripts.

Understanding both the general structure of a place's data model, and how the Roblox engine uses it as the source of truth for a place's state is important for understanding where to store and configure different types of objects. For more information, see data model.

Create games

When you create a new game, it opens a start place that all players will load into when they join the game. The start place represents the overall game until you add additional places for different gameplay areas.

To create a game:

  1. Open Studio.

  2. In the Open a Template section, select a template with the objects you want to start working with for your game, such as:

  3. Baseplate — Starts with a SpawnLocation and a baseplate.

  4. Platformer — Starts with customizable platforms, coin pickups, and double-jump, dashing, rolling, and long jump character mechanics!
  5. Racing — Starts with a working racecar and customizable track objects.

When Studio opens up the template, you now have Place1 that represents your overall game.

Publish games

When you publish a game, Roblox stores the data model of your start place as a .rblx file in the cloud. This is an important process because it connects the game to your account, allowing you to access and work on it from any computer.

By default, new games are only accessible to you as the creator, users with Edit access, and group members with the appropriate roles and permissions. When you are ready to go live to everyone, you can release your game to the public and specify your target audience.

When creating and collaborating on games as part of a group, the ability for group members to playtest/edit/publish games is, by default, dependent on their role permissions. However, group owners or members with sufficient permissions can adjust access on a per‑game level. For more information, see Configure games.

To publish a game for the first time:

  1. In the top-left corner of your computer, navigate to File > Publish. The Game details window displays.

  1. In the window:

  2. Upload an icon and thumbnail to display on your game's main details page.

  3. In the Name field, input the name of your game.
  4. Set Genre and the optional Subgenre dropdown menus to what type of gameplay players should expect. For more information, see Genres.
  5. In the Description field, provide a summary of what players can expect from your game.
  6. Click the Save button. Roblox publishes your game to the cloud with a unique UniverseID.

  1. OPTIONAL You can invite early testers to preview your game.
Metadata best practices

Your game's name and description create an important first impression and contribute to how easily players find your game through Roblox's dynamic discovery systems.

Game name

All games should adhere to the following best practices for naming:

  • Keep the name consistent – Renaming a game too often reduces the chances that players can find it using a previous name.

  • Avoid spamming – Frequent repetition of words or phrases may result in demotion of your game.

Obby Madness

Obby Madness OBBY OBBY OBBY OBBY OBBY

  • Use decorations cautiously – Decorating the name with one or two well-placed emojis isn't harmful, but misplaced or excessive decorations can confuse players who quickly want to identify the game.

🌍 Evolution Simulator 🌍

🐒🐬🐊 Ev🌍luti🌍n Simulator 🌷🍀🌿

Game description

A well-written description promotes the genre and unique qualities of your game while also providing the best context for both players and Roblox's dynamic discovery systems.

  • Summarize your game – Summarize what your game is about in the first sentence, as this is your opportunity to present the most accurate impression of its genre and content.

Compete with racers around the world in some of the craziest courses you've ever seen!

Fight off hordes of zombies with bats, guns, swords, and a bunch of weapons hidden throughout challenging mazes.

  • Provide keywords – Include all keywords that may be relevant to your game. This makes it easier for players and Roblox to understand the themes and genres presented in your game.

Do you enjoy being a sheriff? Join and rid our town of robbers and crooks! Arrest the bad guys, throw them in jail, and even have a guns-blazing shoot-out outside the saloon.

Open your own restaurant, make delicious food, get lots of customers, and expand! Earn experience along the way and learn more recipes. If you love cooking and starting your own business, this is your chance to become a tycoon!

  • Avoid spamming – Avoid repeating keywords or adding irrelevant keywords. This may result in demotion of your game.

Play our fun granny obby game. Obby obby obby obby obby obby obby adopt me bloxburg arsenal ninja legends parkour tycoon battle disaster survival super hero simulator run jump gun rpg pokemon wild west space alien piggy baldi granny murder mystery prison life jail break mario zelda dungeon quest.

Create additional places

After you have published your game, you can add additional places for different gameplay areas. To create a new place within an existing game:

  1. Open an existing place file or create a new place from any Studio template.
  2. Select File > Publish As.
  3. In the Publish Experience window, click the tile for the game you'd like to add the place to.
  4. Select Add as a new place, then click Create.

Whether you choose to have a single, large place or many smaller places is mostly personal preference. For more information, see Design for performance - Streaming and teleportation.

Change start place

The start place of a game cannot be instantly swapped with another place, but you can overwrite the current start place.

To change the start place:

  1. OPTIONAL Save your current start place to a .rbxl file or to a new place within the game.
  2. Navigate to the Creator Dashboard and select the game with the start place that you want to change.
  3. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Configurations > Places.
  4. Click Edit in Studio for the intended new start place. Studio opens and loads that specific place.

  1. In the top-left corner of Studio, go to File > Publish As.
Do not select **Publish** as this would publish the place over itself.
  1. Click the tile for the same game, then choose the current start place. Click Overwrite.

  1. OPTIONAL If the game is live, it's recommended that you restart its servers.

Invite early testers

You can invite up to 10 similar-aged friends to preview your game while you're building it. This allows you to get early feedback before you release your game publicly and receive a content maturity label. For a breakdown of what age ranges can preview your game according to your age, review the following table. If you want to invite someone to preview your game outside of that range, you need to become trusted friends.

Your age Friends you can add Trusted friends you can add
Under 9 N/A N/A
9-12 9-15, plus under-9 friends with parent approval Any age, but under 9 needs parent approval
13-15 9-17 Any age, but under 9 needs parent approval
16-17 13+ Any age, but under 9 needs parent approval
18+ 16+ Any age, but under 9 needs parent approval

When early testers preview a game, they see a watermark that tells them they're in a preview and that Community Standards still apply. In addition, the same in-game reporting and safety tools available in published games stay active, meaning any concerning content or behavior can still be flagged and reviewed even though the game hasn't completed a full content review.

Early testers under 16 can't preview a game rated above the content maturity that their parent allows, and early testers under 18 can't preview a game that has a Restricted maturity label.

To invite early testers to preview your game:

  1. In the top-left corner of your computer, navigate to File > Invite early testers. The Invite early testers window displays.
  2. Using the search bar in the window, select up to 10 similar-aged friends or trusted friends you want to invite to preview your game, then click the Invite button in the bottom-right corner of the window. Each early tester you selected receives an invite to preview your game.

  1. If you have not already completed an age check or age verification, Roblox prompts you to complete an age check.

  2. OPTIONAL You can manage your early testers by clicking the Manage Collaborators button at the top-right corner of Studio. A list of your current early testers displays with the date that you invited them to preview your game. From here, you can:

  3. Add additional early testers by using the search bar.

  4. Remove early testers by clicking the X button in their row.

Release games

By default, the games that you publish are only accessible to you as the creator, users with Edit access, and group members with the appropriate roles and permissions. When you are ready to release your game to additional users, ensure you meet the release requirements below for your target audience, then:

  1. In the top-left corner of your computer, navigate to File > Publish. The Publish window displays.

  2. To invite early testers before you release your game, click the Invite button, otherwise click the Continue button. The window updates with the first question of the Content Maturity questionnaire to see if your game contains age-restricted content.

  3. If your game contains age-restricted content, answer Yes, then complete the entirety of the questionnaire. When you're done, click the Publish button. Your game receives an appropriate content maturity label and content descriptors, and it releases only to age-checked Roblox users ages 16+ or age-verified Roblox users ages 18+, depending on the content within your game.

  4. If your game does not contain age-restricted content, answer No, then click the Publish button. Your game receives a Content May Vary content maturity label, and it releases only to age-checked Roblox users ages 16+. You can later fill out the entirety of the questionnaire on the Creator Hub if you want to expand reach into Roblox Kids, Select, or specific regions requiring more precise maturity rating.

  1. OPTIONAL Grow your audience by either promoting your game with ads or completing age verification to start the process of reaching users under the age of 16 years old.

You can release up to 5 games per day that have never been released before. This limit resets daily. Revoking public access to a released game, then releasing it again does not count toward this limit.

Target audience

You can set a game's target audience on the Creator Hub:

  1. In the Creator Dashboard, select your game.
  2. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Publish settings > Manage Audience.
  3. In the top-right corner, click the Manage access button, then set your target audience using the following tabs and settings:
Tab Settings
Playtest
  • **Early testers** - Your game can only be played by users with **Edit** access and the early testers you invite. This setting is always enabled.
  • **Playtesters** - When enabled, your game is only playable to users with **Edit** or **Playtest** access and the early testers you invite.
Public
  • **Friends** - When enabled, your game can only be played by your friends and those specified in the Playtest tab. When disabled, your game can be played by anyone on Roblox, pending age and geographical restrictions.
  1. Click Save Changes.

  2. OPTIONAL For Public games, you can choose to omit your game from the Recommended For You category on Roblox for more limited reach and exposure.

  3. In the Creator Dashboard, select your game.

  4. Navigate to Audience > Advanced Settings.
  5. In the Recommendations section, toggle Exclude from recommendations.

Release requirements

Release requirements apply to all release actions:

  • Releasing a game for the first time.
  • Updating a released game, such as releasing a new version of a place.
  • Releasing to a different game via Publish As.
  • Changing your target audience settings.

To release a game to ages 16+ and Trusted Friends:

  • Have an account that is in good standing and at least 2 days old.
  • Complete an age check through facial age estimation or government ID.
  • Answer the age-restricted content question that displays first in the Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire:
  • Answer No to receive a Content May Vary label. The game releases only to age-checked Roblox users ages 16+.
  • Answer Yes, then complete the questionnaire. The game receives a label based on your answers and releases to age-checked Roblox users ages 16+ or age-verified Roblox users ages 18+, depending on the content within your game.

To release a game to all ages, including Roblox Kids and Select, you must meet all of the previous requirements plus:

  • Verify your account through facial age estimation if you are under 18 years old, or through government ID if you are 18 years old or older.
  • Enable 2FA on your Roblox account.
  • Meet one of the following:
  • Maintain an active Roblox Plus or Roblox Premium subscription for 2 consecutive months.
  • Pay a one-time, refundable fee.
  • Game must pass the evaluation process for Kids and Select accounts.
  • Complete the entire Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire and receive a Minimal, Mild, or Moderate (9+) content rating.

Optional fees

If you do not have a Roblox Plus or Roblox Premium subscription for 2 consecutive months and you want to release a game to users of all ages, you have the option to pay either a publishing or expedited review fee.

Publishing fee

The publishing fee is a one-time, refundable fee of 1,000 Robux per game that allows you to release and expand the reach of your game to users of all ages. This fee is intended to make it expensive and logistically difficult for bad actors to create large numbers of accounts and flood the platform with spam.

If your game maintains 25 highly engaged players for 60 days without moderation, you will receive a refund of the publishing fee. However, if your game is permanently moderated or taken down for not meeting Roblox's Community Standards within the 60-day period, the fee will not be refunded.

To pay the publishing fee:

  1. In the Creator Hub, select the game you want to release to users of all ages.
  2. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Audience > Reach.
  3. Under Experience reach, navigate to the Refundable publishing fee section, then click the blue Pay button. A pop-up dialog displays.
  4. Click the Pay 1,000 button to confirm your payment.

Expedited review fee

The expedited review fee is a one-time, refundable fee of 50,000 Robux per game that allows you to accelerate the safety and compliance reviews required to release your game to users of all ages. This fee is intended to provide launch flexibility and financial accountability for qualified creators who haven't yet met the highly engaged age-checked player requirement for Kids and Select accounts.

While the expedited review fee accelerates safety and compliance reviews for creators planning a timed launch or running an off-platform campaign and need to know exactly when their game will be ready for all ages, all games must continue to meet the same standards as other Roblox Kids and Select games.

After 90 days, you can request a refund. As long as your game remains in good standing and maintains 25 highly engaged players, you can withdraw your fee and maintain Roblox Kids and Select eligibility. If your game hasn't hit those organic milestones yet, you can leave the fee in place to maintain your eligibility for Kids and Select audiences. However, if your game is permanently moderated or taken down for not meeting Roblox's Community Standards, the fee will not be refunded.

To pay the expedited review fee:

  1. In the Creator Hub, select the game you want to expedite for a safety review.
  2. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Audience > Reach.
  3. Under Experience reach, navigate to the blue alert, then click the gray Pay button. A pop-up dialog displays.
  4. Click the Pay 50,000 button to confirm your payment.

If a minor violation is found during the 48-hour review, you must make the appropriate adjustments to your game, then resubmit. The 48-hour clock restarts from the point of resubmission.

kid.simple: This page shows how to start a new game in Studio, save it online (publish), add more places to it, and finally open it up to other players (release). Publishing and releasing are two different steps: publishing saves your game to Roblox, but only you and your team can play it. Releasing lets the public in, and Roblox has safety rules about who can release to which ages. Knowing these steps helps you share your game with friends first and the whole world later.
kid.analogy: Publishing is like saving your school project to the class drive where only you and your teacher can see it. Releasing is like hanging it on the hallway wall, and the school has rules about which hallway it can go in depending on what is in it.
keyPoints: To create a game, open Studio and pick a template such as Baseplate, Platformer, or Racing. You start with one place called the start place, where every player first spawns.
To publish for the first time, go to File > Publish, add an icon, thumbnail, name, genre, and description, then click Save. Your game is now stored online and linked to your account.

Give your game a clear name and a description whose first sentence says what the game is. Repeating words like OBBY OBBY OBBY or stuffing in unrelated game names can get your game pushed down in search.
To add another place, open or make a place, choose File > Publish As, pick your game, and choose Add as a new place.
To change the start place, open the new place from the Creator Dashboard, use File > Publish As (not Publish), and overwrite the current start place.
Before releasing, you can invite up to 10 similar-aged friends as early testers with File > Invite early testers. They see a preview watermark, and safety and reporting tools still work.

To release, use File > Publish again and answer the content maturity questions. A game with no age-restricted content first gets a Content May Vary label and is shown to age-checked players 16 and up.

Reaching all ages, including younger kids, needs more: account verification, 2-step verification, a passed review, a full questionnaire, and either a Plus or Premium subscription for 2 months in a row or a refundable fee.

terms.publish: Saving your game to Roblox's servers so it is linked to your account and you can open it from any computer. It does not make the game public by itself.
terms.release: Opening your published game so other players (not only you and your team) can join it.
terms.place: One map or level of a game. A game can have a dungeon place, a desert place, and an island place, and players teleport between them.
terms.start place: The place every player loads into first when they join your game.
terms.template: A ready-made starting project, like Baseplate (a flat floor and a spawn point), so you do not start from nothing.
terms.UniverseID: The unique ID number Roblox gives your whole game when you publish it. Each place inside also has its own ID.
terms.metadata: Information about your game, like its name, genre, and description, that helps players and Roblox find it.
terms.Publish As: A menu option that lets you save the place you have open into a different game or over a different place, instead of over itself.
terms.overwrite: Replace something with a new version. The old version is no longer the current one.
terms.early testers: Up to 10 friends you invite to try your game before it is released, so you can get feedback.
terms.content maturity label: A tag like Minimal, Mild, or Moderate that tells players and parents what kind of content is in the game, based on a questionnaire you fill out.
terms.age check: A way Roblox confirms your age, such as a face age estimate or a government ID.
terms.2FA: Two-step verification. Besides your password, you also confirm a code, so it is harder for someone to steal your account.
terms.refundable fee: Robux you pay up front and can get back later if rules are met. For example, the 1,000 Robux publishing fee comes back if your game keeps 25 highly engaged players for 60 days without being moderated.
terms.target audience: Which players are allowed to join, such as only testers, only friends, or everyone.

watchOut: When changing the start place, clicking Publish instead of Publish As just saves the place over itself. Use Publish As and pick the current start place to overwrite.
Expecting your friends to join right after you publish. A newly published game is private until you invite early testers or release it.
Stuffing your description with popular game names to get clicks. Roblox treats this as spam and can demote your game.
Renaming your game often. Players who remember the old name will have a harder time finding it.
You can only release up to 5 brand-new games per day, so plan ahead if you have many.
